speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help you, I need to start by asking about your specific symptoms. Has this pain been present all the time, or does it flare up, and do you feel any burning when you urinate?

Also, have you noticed any blood in your urine, fever, or pain in your back or sides?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor

Thank you for those details; the relief of pain after voiding and worsening over five months are significant clues. Could you describe the exact location of the bladder pain (suprapubic vs. elsewhere), whether the frequency is accompanied by urgency, and if you have noticed any discharge from the urethra?

The clinical picture of chronic suprapubic pain relieved by voiding, urinary frequency, dyspareunia, and absence of infection on urinalysis is classic for this condition.
